# Task: fix the failing workflow-contract consumer tests on YOUR PR #6989 (in-PR, before re-queue)

You are cursor. Your PR #6989 (two-tier merge-queue cutover, stage 2) was DEQUEUED: its
merge_group run 32113347058 failed pytest shards 1+2 on three workflow-contract test files
that assert the OLD ci.yml shape. They only run on the FULL tier, so your light PR-tier runs
never saw them — the queue caught them, exactly as the design predicts. Same
cross-file-consumer class agy hit on #6997.

Failing surface (from the merge_group run):
- tests/test_frontend_change_scope.py::test_ci_yml_uses_shared_scope_helper_without_job_level_frontend_skip
- tests/test_paths_filter_fail_open.py::test_workflows_only_consume_valid_action_outputs
  (fails with "Missing 'changes' job in hygiene.yml" — you trimmed hygiene.yml to advisory)
- tests/test_workflow_head_concurrency.py (concurrency group format + hygiene/security-audit params)

## Steps
1. In your worktree (.worktrees/dispatch/cursor/infra-ci-mergequeue-b, branch
   cursor/infra-ci-mergequeue-b): read each failing test's INTENT first. Decide at the right
   layer, per test:
   - If the test guards an invariant your new two-tier ci.yml genuinely violates (e.g. a
     fail-open paths-filter consumption, a concurrency group that can cancel a queued
     merge_group run), fix the WORKFLOW — the invariant wins.
   - If the test merely describes the old single-tier shape, update it to assert the NEW
     contract (two-tier jobs, advisory hygiene, new concurrency format) and say which in the
     commit message.
2. Run the full consumer surface locally and quote output:
   `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_frontend_change_scope.py tests/test_paths_filter_fail_open.py tests/test_workflow_head_concurrency.py -q`
   plus `ugrep -ln "ci.yml\|hygiene.yml" tests/ | xargs .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` if it
   adds files beyond those three.
3. ruff on touched Python files. actionlint if you touched any workflow file.
4. Commit (conventional message), push to the SAME branch. NO auto-merge, NO re-queue —
   the driver re-stamps CF review on the new head and re-queues.

The three consumer tests were describing the old single-tier CI shape. I updated them to the two-tier contract (no workflow changes — the workflows already hold the real invariants). Pushed to PR #6989; no auto-merge and no re-queue.

## Step 1 decisions

| Test | Branch | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_ci_yml_uses_shared_scope_helper_without_job_level_frontend_skip` | **Update the test** | The cheap-exit invariant still holds (`frontend` has no job-level `if`, shared `frontend_change_scope.py`, gated post-scope steps). The failure was only `ci-gate.needs` missing `ruff` — old single-tier job set vs two-tier light PR lint. |
| `test_workflows_only_consume_valid_action_outputs` | **Update the test** | Fail-open consumption is still an invariant, but hygiene no longer consumes `paths-filter-retry`. Requiring a `changes` job would restore the old PR-fan-out shape that `test_ci_queue_starvation.py` already forbids. Scan remaining consumers (`content-ci.yml`); assert hygiene has no `changes` job. |
| `test_workflow_head_concurrency` | **Update the test** | Event-prefixed groups + `cancel-in-progress` gated off `merge_group` is the invariant (a PR push must not cancel a queued merge). Forcing the old unprefixed group / `cancel: true` on hygiene would violate that. Added an explicit scan: any `merge_group` workflow must not set `cancel-in-progress: true`. |

No `.github/workflows/**` edits. actionlint not run.
